The '''2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Michigan]] during the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Wolverines, led by head coach [[John Beilein]] in his 11th year, played their home games for the 51st consecutive year at the [[Crisler Center]] in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]]. This season marked the program's 102nd season and its 101st consecutive year as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]].

The entering class included 2017 Michigan [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards#Basketball|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]] [[Isaiah Livers]]. Kentucky transfer [[Charles Matthews (basketball)|Charles Matthews]] became eligible to play this season after sitting out the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], while graduate transfer [[Jaaron Simmons]] became eligible to play immediately. The departing class included graduating seniors [[Zak Irvin]] and [[Derrick Walton]] who had completed their eligibility, and graduating seniors Mark Donnal and [[Andrew Dakich]]. In addition, [[D. J. Wilson]] declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]] with two years of eligibility remaining. [[Jeff Meyer (basketball)|Jeff Meyer]] and [[Billy Donlon]] also departed prior to the season to take assistant coaching positions at [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]] and [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]], respectively, and were replaced by [[DeAndre Haynes]] and Luke Yaklich.

During the regular season, the team finished tied for fourth in the [[2017–18 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten Conference]]. They earned a 5th seed in the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]], where they won the championship, thus defending the title won by the [[2016–17 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2016–17 Wolverines]] in the [[2017 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]] the year before. The Wolverines finished the season with a 33–8 record, setting a program record for wins during a season. The team earned the third seed in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] and reached the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|Championship Game]] before losing to [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]].

==Regular season==

===November===
Michigan began the season with a victory over [[2017–18 North Florida Ospreys men's basketball team|North Florida]]. Although the game was tied with 11:03 remaining, Michigan won 86–66. Michigan was led by [[Duncan Robinson (basketball)|Duncan Robinson]] with a game-high 21 points, while [[Charles Matthews (basketball)|Charles Matthews]] posted 20 points in his Michigan debut, marking the first time Michigan had two 20-point scorers since March 3, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986333|title=Michigan pulls away late for 86–66 win over North Florida|access-date=November 12, 2017|date=November 11, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/news/2017/11/11/mens-basketball-wolverines-use-second-half-burst-to-down-north-florida-in-2017-18-opener.aspx|title=Wolverines Use Second-Half Burst to Down North Florida in 2017–18 Opener|access-date=November 12, 2017|date=November 11, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 13, Michigan defeated [[2017–18 Central Michigan Chippewas men's basketball team|Central Michigan]] 72–65. Michigan had five double-digit scorers, including [[Muhammad-Ali Abdur-Rahkman]] who led the team with 17 points and [[Moe Wagner]] who contributed his second consecutive [[double-double]], and third of his career. With seven lead changes in the game, Michigan took the lead for good with 8:47 remaining.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986344|title=Abdur-Rahkman scores 17 in Michigan's 72–65 win over Chips|access-date=November 14, 2017|date=November 13, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/news/2017/11/13/mens-basketball-wolverines-grind-out-win-over-chippewas-in-in-state-tilt.aspx|title=Wolverines Grind Out Win Over Chippewas in In-State Tilt|access-date=November 14, 2017|date=November 13, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 16, [[Jon Teske]], who had previous career highs of four points and three rebounds, led Michigan with a 10-point, 11-rebound double-double as Michigan overcame its third second-half deficit in three games against [[2017–18 Southern Miss Golden Eagles basketball team|Southern Miss]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986356|title=Teske lifts Michigan to 61–47 win over Southern Miss|access-date=November 17, 2017|date=November 16, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

In the first round of the [[2017 Maui Invitational Tournament]] (its fifth) on November 20, against [[2017–18 LSU Tigers basketball team|Louisiana State]], Michigan overcame an eight-point deficit with 12 minutes remaining to take a nine-point lead with five minutes remaining only to lose 77–75.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986374|title=LSU rallies late for 77–75 win over Michigan in Maui|access-date=November 21, 2017|date=November 21, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/news/2017/11/21/mens-basketball-wolverines-rally-against-lsu-falls-just-short-in-maui-opener.aspx|title=Wolverines' Rally Against LSU Falls Just Short in Maui Opener|access-date=November 21, 2017|date=November 21, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> In the consolation bracket, Michigan defeated {{cbb link|2017|sex=men|team=Chaminade Silverswords|school=Chaminade University of Honolulu|title=Chaminade}} the next day on the strength of Matthews' first career double-double (22 points and 10 rebounds). Michigan set or tied school single-game tournament records in scoring margin (38), field-goal percentage (64.9), assists (22), three-pointers made (15), three-point attempts (28), three-point percentage (53.6), steals (nine), turnover low (eight) and blocks (six).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401000094|title=Michigan rolls over Chaminade 102–64 at Maui Invitational|access-date=November 22, 2017|date=November 21, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/news/2017/11/21/mens-basketball-michigan-rolls-past-chaminade-at-maui-invitational.aspx|title=Michigan Rolls Past Chaminade at Maui Invitational|access-date=November 22, 2017|date=November 21, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 22, Michigan defeated [[2017–18 VCU Rams men's basketball team|Virginia Commonwealth]] (VCU) 68–60, earning a fifth-place finish in the Maui Invitational Tournament. Michigan was led by Robinson with a game-high 18 points. Michigan trailed by three points with two minutes remaining, before the Wolverines outscored VCU 11–0 down the stretch.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401000097|title=Michigan beats VCU 68–60 for fifth in Maui|access-date=November 22, 2017|date=November 22, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/news/2017/11/22/mens-basketball-wolverines-outlast-vcu-in-final-maui-matchup.aspx|title=Wolverines Outlast VCU in Final Maui Matchup|access-date=November 22, 2017|date=November 22, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>  On November 26, Michigan defeated [[2017–18 UC Riverside Highlanders men's basketball team|UC Riverside]]  87–42 on the strength of double-doubles by Wagner (21 points, 10 rebounds) and Matthews (17 points, 12 assists). It was the team's first pair of double-doubles in a game since [[Glenn Robinson III]] and [[Trey Burke]] did so for the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2012–13 National Runner-up Wolverines]] on January 6, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986393|title=Wagner's double-double leads Michigan past UC Riverside|access-date=November 27, 2017|date=November 26, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/news/2017/11/26/mens-basketball-wolverines-dominate-uc-riverside-in-wire-to-wire-win.aspx|title=Wolverines Dominate UC Riverside in Wire-to-Wire Win|access-date=November 27, 2017|date=November 26, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 29, Michigan lost to (#13 [[AP Poll]]/#11 [[Coaches Poll]]) [[2017–18 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] 86–71 in the [[ACC–Big Ten Challenge]]. Michigan was led by Wagner with a team-high 20 points. This was the first meeting between the two teams since the [[1993 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986105|title=No. 13 UNC beats Michigan 86–71 in Big Ten/ACC Challenge|access-date=November 29, 2017|date=November 29, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/news/2017/11/29/mens-basketball-wolverines-drop-b1g-acc-challenge-matchup-at-no-13-north-carolina.aspx|title=Wolverines Drop B1G/ACC Challenge Matchup at No. 13 North Carolina|access-date=November 29, 2017|date=November 29, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref>

===December===
The [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|2018 Big Ten tournament]] was held at [[Madison Square Garden]] in [[New York City]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2014/12/09/big-ten-tournament-at-msg-in-2018/20156595/|title=Big Ten tournament at MSG in 2018|work=USA Today|access-date=2017-04-14|language=en}}</ref> Due to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]]'s use of that venue for the [[2018 Big East men's basketball tournament|2018 Big East tournament]], the Big Ten tournament took place one week earlier than usual, ending the week before Selection Sunday.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/here-are-the-top-10-games-on-the-big-tens-weird-2017-18-conference-schedule/|title=Here are the top 10 games on the Big Ten's weird 2017–18 conference schedule|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-08-18|language=en}}</ref> As a result, each team played one road game and one home conference game in the first week of December.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/here-are-the-top-10-games-on-the-big-tens-weird-2017-18-conference-schedule/|title=Here are the top 10 games on the Big Ten's weird 2017–18 conference schedule|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-08-18|language=en}}</ref>

On December 2, Michigan defeated [[2017–18 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] 69–55 in its Big Ten conference opener. Jordan Poole led the team with a career-high 19 points, while Muhammad-Ali Abdur Rahkman added eight points and a career-high 11 rebounds, and Eli Brooks added five points and a career-high six assists.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986396|title=Quick start lifts Michigan to 69–55 win over Indiana|access-date=December 2, 2017|date=December 2, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/news/2017/12/2/mens-basketball-wolverines-roll-past-indiana-in-big-ten-home-opener.aspx|title=Wolverines Roll Past Indiana in Big Ten Home Opener|access-date=December 2, 2017|date=December 2, 2017|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> Two days later, Michigan lost to [[2017–18 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] 71–62, after leading by as many as 20 points with 1:31 remaining in the first half. ==Postseason==
===Big Ten tournament===
On March 1, Michigan opened its [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]] play with a 77–71 overtime victory over Iowa. Michigan survived a rough shooting night (56% on free throws and 16% three-point field goals) and foul trouble (Wagner and Abdur-Rahkman [[Personal foul (basketball)#Fouling out|fouled out]]) to get the victory. Matthews led the way with 16 points, but Robinson made the go ahead three point shot with 2:17 remaining in overtime and the sank two free throws to give Michigan a two-possession lead with 10 seconds remaining.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020033|title=No. 15 Michigan overcomes Iowa in OT 77–71 in Big Ten|access-date=March 1, 2018|date=March 1, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/1/mens-basketball-michigan-grinds-out-overtime-win-over-iowa-in-big-ten-tournament-opener.aspx|title=Michigan Grinds Out Overtime Win Over Iowa in Big Ten tournament Opener|access-date=March 1, 2018|date=March 1, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030118aaf.html|title=Postgame Notes: Michigan-Iowa|access-date=March 2, 2018|date=March 1, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=BigTen.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302164032/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030118aaf.html|archive-date=March 2, 2018|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

The next day, Michigan defeated Nebraska 77–58 in the quarterfinals of the Big Ten tournament. Michigan was led by Abdur-Rahkman with 21 points, while Wagner recorded his seventh double-double of the season with 20 points and 13 rebounds. Michigan's defense held Nebraska to just 30% shooting for the game (16-of-53), including 1-of-20 during a 13:32 stretch in the first half. Robinson scored his 1,000th career point on his second 3-point field goal of the first half. Abdur-Rahkman (5–5) became the second player in the history of the [[Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]] to be perfect on at least 5 three-point shots in a single game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020037|title=No. 15 Michigan deals blow to Nebraska's NCAA hopes, 77–58|access-date=March 2, 2018|date=March 2, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/2/mens-basketball-wagners-double-double-guides-michigan-past-nebraska-into-b1g-tournament-semis.aspx|title=Wagner's Double-Double Guides Michigan Past Nebraska, Into B1G Tournament Semis|access-date=March 2, 2018|date=March 2, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030218aag.html|title=Postgame Notes: Michigan-Nebraska|access-date=March 2, 2018|date=March 2, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=BigTen.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303110209/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030218aag.html|archive-date=March 3, 2018|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref> On March 3, Michigan defeated (#2 AP Poll/#2 Coaches Poll) Michigan State 75–64 in the semifinals of the Big Ten tournament. With the win, Michigan advanced to the Big Ten tournament final for the second consecutive season, and snapped Michigan State's 13-game winning streak. Michigan was led by Abdur-Rahkman, Simpson and Wagner with 15 points each. Wagner scored his 1,000th career point in the second half of the game, becoming the 54th Wolverine to reach the milestone.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020040|title=Michigan ends top-seeded Spartans' 13-game winning streak|access-date=March 3, 2018|date=March 3, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/3/mens-basketball-downs-spartans-advances-to-b1g-tournament-final.aspx|title=Wolverines Down Spartans, Advance to B1G Tournament Final|access-date=March 3, 2018|date=March 3, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030318aad.html|title=Postgame Notes: Michigan-Michigan State|access-date=March 3, 2018|date=March 3, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=BigTen.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304113247/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030318aad.html|archive-date=March 4, 2018|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

On March 4, Michigan defeated (#8 AP Poll/#8 Coaches Poll) Purdue 75–66 to claim their second consecutive Big Ten tournament championship. They became the first fifth seed to win the championship and the first team to win consecutive tournament championships since Ohio State in [[2009–10 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|2010]] and [[2010–11 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|2011]]. Michigan was led by Wagner with a team-high 17 points, and was named tournament MVP, while Abdur-Rahkman recorded 15 points and was named to the All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020042|title=Michigan beats Purdue to win 2nd straight Big Ten tournament|access-date=March 4, 2018|date=March 4, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref name=BWTPMtSSBTT>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/4/mens-basketball-back-to-back-wagner-teske-power-michigan-to-second-straight-b1g-tournament-title.aspx|title=Back-to-Back: Wagner, Teske Power Michigan to Second Straight B1G Tournament Title|access-date=March 4, 2018|date=March 4, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030418aab.html|title=Postgame Notes: Michigan-Purdue|access-date=March 5, 2018|date=March 4, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=BigTen.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180305142711/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030418aab.html|archive-date=March 5, 2018|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

===NCAA tournament===
On March 15, Michigan began their participation in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]] with a 61–47 victory over [[2017–18 Montana Grizzlies basketball team|Montana]] in the first round. Michigan was led by Matthews with 20 points and a career-tying 11 rebounds, for his fourth double-double of the season. After Montana jumped out to an early 10–0 lead, Michigan's defense held Montana to just 32.1% shooting for the game, including 1-of-14 during a ten-minute stretch to start the second half. The second half was delayed for over 10 minutes with 17:53 remaining when the [[shot clock]]s lost power.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025838|title=Michigan plods to 61–47 win over Montana in NCAA first round|access-date=March 16, 2018|date=March 16, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/16/mens-basketball-michigan-eases-into-ncaa-second-round-with-win-over-montana.aspx|title=Michigan Eases into NCAA Second Round with Win Over Montana|access-date=March 16, 2018|date=March 16, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref>

On March 17, Michigan defeated (#21 AP Poll/#19 Coaches Poll) [[2017–18 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] 64–63 in the second round, following a game-winning [[buzzer beater]] [[three-point shot]] by Poole as time expired. Abdur-Rahkman and Wagner led the scoring with 12 points each. There were 17 lead changes and 12 ties during the game, while neither team ever led by more than six points. With the win, Michigan advanced to its fourth Sweet 16 in six years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025868|title=Poole's buzzer-beating sends Michigan past Houston, 64–63|access-date=March 18, 2018|date=March 18, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/18/mens-basketball-march-madness-poole-sends-michigan-to-sweet-16.aspx|title=March Madness: Poole Sends Michigan to Sweet 16|access-date=March 18, 2018|date=March 18, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> On March 22, Michigan defeated [[2017–18 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] 99–72 in the regional semifinals. Abdur-Rahkman led with 24 points, while Wagner added 21 points, and Matthews 18 points. Michigan made 10 of its 14 three-pointers in the first half to take a 52–28 lead at halftime. Eight different Wolverines made a three-point field goal, setting a program record for most players to make one in an NCAA tournament game. Michigan posted 12 steals, including a career-high six by Simpson, which tied a Michigan NCAA tournament record. Michigan's 99 points were the sixth most in program history in the NCAA tournament, and the most they've scored since scoring 102 against [[1991–92 East Tennessee State Buccaneers men's basketball team|East Tennessee]] in [[1992 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1992]]. Michigan's 61.9% shooting was its second-best in program history in the NCAA tournament. With the win, Michigan advanced to its third Elite Eight in six years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025875|title=Streaking Michigan routs Texas A&M 99–72 in West semifinals|access-date=March 22, 2018|date=March 22, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/22/mens-basketball-michigan-proves-elite-in-27-point-win-over-texas-am.aspx|title=Michigan Proves Elite in 27-Point Win over Texas A&M|access-date=March 22, 2018|date=March 22, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/23/mens-basketball-wolverines-to-face-no-9-seed-florida-state-for-spot-in-ncaa-final-four.aspx|title=Wolverines to Face No. 9 Seed Florida State for Spot in NCAA Final Four|access-date=March 24, 2018|date=March 23, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref>

On March 24, Michigan defeated [[2017–18 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] 58–54 in the regional finals. Michigan was led by Matthews with 17 points. With the win, Michigan advances to the Final Four for the eighth time in program history and for the first time since [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013]]. Michigan set a single-season program record with its 32nd victory of the season, surpassing the previous record of 31 wins set by the [[1992–93 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1992–93]] and [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2012–13 teams]]. Michigan's defense held Florida State to just 23.3% (7-of-30) shooting in the second half.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025885|title=Oh Blue!: Michigan nips Florida St 58–54 to reach Final Four|access-date=March 25, 2018|date=March 24, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/24/mens-basketball-hello-final-four-michigans-defense-reigns-against-florida-state.aspx|title=Hello, Final Four! Michigan's Defense Reigns Against Florida State|access-date=March 25, 2018|date=March 24, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> Matthews was named West Region Most Outstanding Player and was joined on the West Region All-tournament team by Wagner and Abdur-Rahkman.<ref name=atMMsu>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/marchmadness/status/978070719773986816|title=@MarchMadness status update|publisher=[[NCAA]]|access-date=March 26, 2018|date=March 25, 2018}}</ref> With the Wolverines men's basketball team advancing to the Final Four and the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's ice hockey season|2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's ice hockey team]] advancing to the Frozen Four, it was the fourth time that both programs made their respective final four tournaments during the same season, and just the sixth time overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/25/ice-hockey-michigan-clinches-trip-to-25th-frozen-four-with-win-over-bu.aspx|title=Michigan Clinches Trip to 25th Frozen Four with Win Over BU|access-date=March 25, 2018|date=March 25, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Garske, TJ}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2018/03/25/michigan-makes-double-final-fours/33284279/|title=Michigan makes it a double on final fours|access-date=March 26, 2018|date=March 26, 2018|work=[[The Detroit News]]|author=Paul, Tony}}</ref>

On March 31, Michigan defeated [[2017–18 Loyola Ramblers men's basketball team|Loyola–Chicago]] 69–57 in the national semifinals. Michigan was led by Wagner with 24 points and a career-high 15 rebounds, for his eighth double-double of the season, while Matthews added 17 points. Wagner became the third player with at least 20 points and 15 rebounds in a national semifinal game, and the first to do so since [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] in [[1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1983]]. Michigan thus advanced to its seventh national championship game, and first since [[2013 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|2013]], and set a single season record with its 33rd victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025887|title=Wagner, Michigan end Loyola's run 69–57 in Final Four|access-date=March 31, 2018|date=March 31, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/31/mens-basketball-wolverines-take-down-loyola-chicago-to-advance-to-ncaa-championship-game.aspx|title=Wolverines Take Down Loyola Chicago to Advance to NCAA Championship Game|access-date=March 31, 2018|date=March 31, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref>

On April 2, Michigan lost to (#2 Coaches Poll/#2 AP Poll) [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] 79–62 in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|National Championship Game]]. The loss snapped Michigan's 14-game win streak that dated back to February 6, and was the longest active winning streak in the nation. This was Michigan's longest winning streak since winning the first 16 games to start the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/4/1/mens-basketball-michigan-set-to-face-villanova-for-national-championship.aspx?path=mbball|title=Michigan Set to Face Villanova for National Championship|access-date=April 1, 2018|date=April 1, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> Michigan was led by Abdur-Rahkman with 23 points, who finished his collegiate career as Michigan's all-time leader in games played with 144 games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025888|title=Villanova takes title, 79–62 over Michigan behind DiVincenzo|access-date=April 3, 2018|date=April 3, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/4/2/mens-basketball-michigan-comes-up-short-against-villanova-in-national-championship-game.aspx|title=Michigan Comes Up Short Against Villanova in National Championship Game|access-date=April 3, 2018|date=April 2, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> Wagner was Michigan's only representative on the Final Four All-Tournament Team.<ref name=MWCMhdtmaND>{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2018/04/03/moritz-wagner-charles-matthews-have-decisions-make-nba-draft/33501655/|title=Moritz Wagner, Charles Matthews have decisions to make about NBA Draft|access-date=April 5, 2018|date=April 3, 2018|work=[[Detroit News]]|author=Hawkins, James}}</ref>

With the loss to Villanova, Michigan's record in the national championship game fell to 1–6, the worst record among teams that have previously won a national championship. This was the fourth consecutive loss in the championship game for the Wolverines since their sole title in [[1989 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|1989]], having previously lost in [[1992 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|1992]], [[1993 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|1993]], and [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|2013]].
